hook.text: Modern corn looks nothing like its ancestor — teosinte had tiny ears with just a dozen kernels.

buildup.text: For 9,000 years, farmers saved seeds from the best plants — slowly reshaping crops generation by generation.

discovery.text: Selective breeding changes DNA without touching it directly — nature provides mutations, humans pick winners.

twist.text: Dogs, from chihuahuas to Great Danes, are all one species — bred from wolves in just 15,000 years.

climax.text: Modern breeding uses DNA markers to accelerate selection — combining ancient practice with genomic precision.

punchline.text: Every farm crop is a biotech product — shaped by millennia of human choice.

quiz.question: What is the wild ancestor of modern corn?
options: Wild wheat from the Fertile Crescent
Teosinte, a grass with tiny ears and few kernels

details.summary: Selective breeding is the oldest form of biotechnology, where humans choose organisms with desirable traits to reproduce over many generations. This process transformed wild grasses into modern wheat, wolves into dog breeds, and wild fowl into productive poultry.
details.whyItMatters: Selective breeding created virtually all modern crops and livestock, enabling civilization itself. Understanding it as humanity's first genetic technology provides context for modern genetic engineering as an accelerated continuation of the same
takeaways: Selective breeding chooses organisms with desired traits for reproduction
Thousands of years of selection transformed wild ancestors into modern crops
Modern genetic engineering accelerates what breeding achieves over generations

faq.question: How long did selective breeding take to create modern crops?
faq.answer: Maize was domesticated from teosinte grass over several thousand years in Mexico. Modern wheat resulted from thousands of years of selection and natural hybridization events. Dog breeds diversified over roughly 15,000 years of selection from wolf ancestors.

faq.question: How is selective breeding different from genetic engineering?
faq.answer: Selective breeding shuffles existing natural variation across whole genomes through reproduction and selection. Genetic engineering precisely inserts, removes, or modifies specific genes with known functions. Breeding is slower but changes many traits simultaneously.
